full_judgment: 19. In the case of New Zealand Insurance Co. Ltd., Chittagong.tvs. M.A. Rouf & ors., 13 DLR 186, the point of limitation was elaborately discussed. The facts of that case were similar to those of the instant case. In that case the plaintiff had imported goods from Belgium, which were shipped from Antwerp to the port of Chattogram in Bangladesh and were discharged before the vessel left Chattogram on 10.6.52. The suit was filed on 10.8.53 claiming that it was filed within the period of limitation since the certificate showing short landing was issued on 07.03.1953. The question of applicability of the Hague Visby Rules were discussed at length. The High Court Division observed that the rules relating to bills of lading contained in the International Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules of Law relating to Bills of Lading ("Hague Rules") were included in a schedule to the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925 (the Act, 1925). It was further observed that the Act, as in force in Pakistan, applies to the carriage of goods by sea from any port in Pakistan to any other port whether in or outside Pakistan, but does not apply to the carriage of goods by sea from a foreign port to a port in Pakistan as provided in section 2 of that Act, 1925.
